title: M/s K.L. Concast Pvt. Ltd. v. Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.
coram: Sunita Agarwal, J.; Jayant Banerji, J.
disposition: Time granted for counter and rejoinder; listed 4 January 2021.
headnote: Allahabad High Court (Sunita Agarwal and Jayant Banerji, JJ.) granted the licensee three weeks to file a counter affidavit and one week thereafter for rejoinder on a writ alleging delay of more than six months in determining a load-reduction request under Section 43 of the Electricity Act, 2003 and Clause 4.41(b) of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005, and listed the matter on 4 January 2021. Those provisions were not construed.
facts: The petitioners, M/s K.L. Concast Pvt. Ltd. and another, filed a writ petition against Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Limited complaining that the licensee took more than six months to determine their request for reduction of load. They alleged that the delay ran contrary to Section 43 of the Electricity Act, 2003 read with Clause 4.41(b) of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005. At the first listing, counsel for the Corporation sought time to file a counter affidavit.

holding_units.topic: interlocutory listing; load-reduction delay not decided
holding_units.holding: The Division Bench granted the licensee three weeks to file a counter affidavit and one week thereafter for the petitioners' rejoinder, and listed the writ on 4 January 2021. The complaint that determination of a load-reduction request took more than six months contrary to Section 43 of the Electricity Act, 2003 and Clause 4.41(b) of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 was not adjudicated.

principle_tags.application: Writ alleging delay in deciding a load-reduction request under Section 43 and Clause 4.41(b) was adjourned for pleadings without any construction of those provisions.

not_decided.point: Whether delay of more than six months in determining a load-reduction request violated Section 43 of the Electricity Act, 2003 and Clause 4.41(b) of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005.
not_decided.note: Only time for counter and rejoinder was granted; merits not heard.
